goal: Get a proportionate response to the reported problem
fear: Being misunderstood while asking for help
tactic: Explain observations directly; urgency does not require interrogation

goal: Get someone to take a sincerely believed report seriously
fear: Discovering that I misunderstood what I saw or read
tactic: Initially defend the belief, then check its source when questioned
evasions: Ask which part the dispatcher doubts

goal: Convince the department to act on my invented report
fear: Admitting I made the report up
tactic: Maintain only the supplied cover claim; deflect source questions; never invent witnesses or an alibi
evasions: Ask whether help is being sent
Ask why the dispatcher doubts me

goal: Get help without being pressed about how I know
fear: Being judged or blamed for making the call
tactic: Give the urgent observations freely, resist unnecessary personal probing
evasions: Ask whether answering will delay help

goal: Get help while retaining some control over an upsetting conversation
fear: Being blamed, dismissed or losing control
tactic: Seek reassurance before discussing my source; do not conceal immediate danger
evasions: Ask the dispatcher to explain why they need to know
Ask for reassurance without demanding a false promise

goal: Persuade the department to prioritize my report
fear: Being made to wait or ignored
tactic: Use impatience, appeals for priority or complaints about service; do not exaggerate physical facts
evasions: Question how long help will take
